text: 🇲🇽🌎 70% of Mexico's territory is forest. 12% of the world's biodiversity is in Mexico. 60% of forest ecosystems sit on communal and ejidal land. — Alicia Bárcena, Environment Secretary The challenges: 203,552 hectares deforested every year, 846,357 hit by forest fires, 62,038 by pests — and illegal logging as the biggest threat, now being tackled jointly with the Security Secretariat. Sunday's National Reforestation Jornada is the first of an annual series.

🇲🇽🏠 "We have already placed more than 33,000 homes with beneficiaries. And this August we will open 14 more developments across the country." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Infonavit director Housing Wednesday #27, live from Querétaro — the 21st state covered. Infonavit is delivering in 112 housing developments; 39 are already 100% placed. In Querétaro, 16,740 homes are underway, 35% of the state goal. Tatiana, a working mother of three, got her keys today: "Trust it, file your paperwork — you can have your house."

🇲🇽🌱 "There is no other program like Sembrando Vida in the world — one that gives monthly support to the sowers themselves." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo In 8 years, Sembrando Vida has planted 1.2 billion timber and fruit trees and reforested 1 million hectares, run by 417,000+ sowers. Budget: ~35 billion pesos a year. A general evaluation is underway to expand it — and Sheinbaum called on citizens to report any extortion inside the program, and pledged to seek social security for its sowers.

🇲🇽🌳 "The goal is for this Jornada to happen every year — not just 2026. One day a year when all of us reforest." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo On Sunday, Aug 9, Mexico holds its first National Reforestation Jornada — now an annual event: 6.6 million trees and plants in a single day, across all 32 states, 621 municipalities, with 235,097 participants. Sheinbaum will plant in Izta-Popo National Park, Puebla. Goal: 1.5 billion trees reforested or conserved by 2030.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO’S INVESTMENT: ONE COOL MONTH, ONE CLIMBING YEAR</u>

Gross fixed investment in Mexico dipped 0.4% in May after two straight months of growth, El Economista reports — construction cooled 2.4% after surging 6.5% in April.

Zoom out: INEGI’s data shows investment up 1.1% year-on-year in May and holding its upward trend. The headline-writers quoting a single monthly print won’t mention that.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>MEXICO’S STATE LOTTERY HONORS 24 FUTBOL LEGENDS</u>

In World Cup year, the Lotería Nacional — the state lottery whose proceeds fund public causes — presented “Leyendas del Futbol,” a commemorative ticket series honoring 24 former Mexican national team players who made history.

While FIFA’s billion-dollar machine squeezes host cities for more, Mexico puts its football memory in people’s hands for the price of a cachito.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM PLAYS THE TAPE: MEXICO’S MEDIA STARS, 26 YEARS OF HYPOCRISY</u>

In the year 2000, on Canal 40’s Séptimo Día, Mexico’s star journalists — Carmen Aristegui, Joaquín López-Dóriga, Ciro Gómez Leyva, Sergio Sarmiento, Denise Maerker — sat together agreeing that mechanisms were needed to protect audiences from false information in the media.

Today the same voices cry “censorship” over guidelines that guarantee exactly those audience rights. So Sheinbaum played the 26-year-old clip at the mañanera and called it by its name: hypocrisy. The receipts still burn.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND BRAZIL BACK BACHELET FOR THE UN, AS CEPAL MAPS EIGHT RUPTURES OF THE GLOBAL ORDER</u>

CEPAL presented its report on geopolitics, globalization and development, identifying eight ruptures now tearing at the global order and conditioning every development strategy in the Americas. Delivering the diagnosis: Michelle Bachelet — Chile’s candidate for UN Secretary-General, backed by Mexico and Brazil.

Latin America isn’t waiting for Washington to define the next world order. It is writing the analysis and proposing the leadership.
banner: MEXICO & BRAZIL BACK BACHELET FOR UN

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MORENA OPENS SANCTIONS AGAINST ITS OWN DEPUTIES WHO MOCKED THE ELDERLY</u>

No impunity inside the 4T. Morena’s national leadership opened a disciplinary process against Puebla deputies Nayeli Salvatori and Grace Palomares and asked for their political rights to be suspended, after the two joked on their podcast “Descasadas” that old people “smell like a trunk.”

Sheinbaum’s verdict was blunt: “It is not correct.” The party that made the seniors’ pension universal doesn’t protect anyone who laughs at the people who built this country — not even its own.
banner: MORENA SANCTIONS DEPUTIES FOR MOCKING ELDERLY

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM TO THE VATICAN: POPE LEO XIV MUST COME TO MEXICO</u>

President Sheinbaum met for over an hour at Palacio Nacional with Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican’s Secretary of State, and pressed Mexico’s standing invitation: Pope Leo XIV should visit Mexico. “We are going to insist on the Pope’s visit to Mexico,” she said — she spoke with him directly on December 12 and had already sent a formal letter.

She also praised his AI encyclical Magnifica Humanitas as “a world reference” for the debate Mexico is already waging: who controls the platforms, who designs the algorithms, where humanity is headed. Nearly 100 million Catholics live in Mexico — the second-largest Catholic population on earth. The Holy See is listening.
banner: SHEINBAUM TO POPE LEO XIV: COME TO MEXICO
